summary: Read an integer n in the range from 1 to 50. Using only the five vowels a, e, i, o, and u, count the strings of length n that never descend in dictionary order. Never descending means that, apart from the final letter, every letter is either identical to its right-hand neighbor or stands earlier in the alphabet than that neighbor. Write how many strings meet the length and the order rule.
notes: The left column is this sample's input text and the right column is the text the program should print. Comparison ignores trailing newlines.
